note: Sample data made up for this demo: the restaurants, ratings and free tables are invented, and the photos are illustrations. No live search or booking happened.

idea.title: Dinner date next Friday
idea.text:
Find a restaurant for a date next Friday, 6 November, around 19:30 in Amsterdam.

- We like **Japanese, French, Asian and Spanish** food
- Somewhere quiet enough to talk, about €50–90 a head
- Show me which ones still have a table, where they are on a map, and plenty of photos of the food and the room

agents.title: Find Japanese and French places
agents.text: Search for Japanese and French restaurants in central Amsterdam that suit a date: reviews, price, the room, and how to book.

places.name: Kumo Izakaya
places.about: A busy izakaya with a long counter and a few booths at the back. Small plates to share: grilled black cod, chicken skewers, chawanmushi.
places.date: Ask for a booth: the counter is fun but loud.

places.name: Hana Omakase
places.about: Ten seats around one chef. A fixed omakase of twelve courses, mostly nigiri.
places.date: Special, but booked out four weeks ahead.

places.name: Sora Ramen & Sake
places.about: Rich tonkotsu ramen and a long sake list. Quick, warm and casual.
places.date: No bookings, walk in only; usually a queue on Fridays.

places.name: Le Petit Canal
places.about: A candle-lit bistro in a canal-house basement. Steak frites, duck confit, a short list of Loire wines.
places.date: Ask for the window table on the canal.

places.name: Maison Lumière
places.about: Modern French tasting menu in a bright room near the Museumplein.
places.date: Only a 21:30 waitlist left for Friday.

places.name: Café Margaux
places.about: A small wine bar and bistro by the Hortus. Cheese, terrine, and one dish of the day.
places.date: Relaxed and quiet, good for talking.

places.name: Jade Garden
places.about: Cantonese, with dim sum served into the evening and a roast duck worth the trip.
places.date: Lively, big round tables; ask for a table for two by the window.

places.name: Saigon Lanterns
places.about: Vietnamese with paper lanterns and a small courtyard. Pho, crispy rice pancakes, lemongrass beef.

places.name: Bangkok Kitchen Club
places.about: Thai, cooked over charcoal in an open kitchen. Green curry, grilled pork neck, mango sticky rice.
places.date: A little further out, by tram 9 from Centraal.

places.name: Taberna Sol
places.about: Tapas and vermouth in a narrow room with tiles from Seville. Croquetas, gambas al ajillo, Iberian ham.
places.date: Book the 20:00 slot: the bar is calmer after the after-work crowd.

places.name: Casa Mar
places.about: Seafood and paella for two on the water, with a terrace heater outside.
places.date: Fully booked on Friday; Saturday is open.

places.name: Bodega Luna
places.about: Natural wine and small plates from northern Spain, in a corner bodega.
places.date: Fine, though reviews mention slow service on busy nights.

pick.title: Friday plan: Le Petit Canal at 19:30
pick.text:
**First choice: Le Petit Canal, 19:30.** French bistro on the Prinsengracht, about €65 a head, rated 4.6. A few tables left at 19:30; ask for the window table on the canal. Quiet enough to talk.

**If it goes: Kumo Izakaya, 19:30.** Japanese small plates in De Pijp, about €55, rated 4.6. Ask for a booth.

**Something different: Taberna Sol, 20:00.** Spanish tapas in the Jordaan, about €45, rated 4.5.

**Set aside:** Hana Omakase, Maison Lumière and Casa Mar are fully booked on Friday; Sora Ramen takes no bookings.

In the app, an agent with a booking plugin could reserve the table once you say which one.
